high: Laugh and say your results are hit-or-miss, then ask about someone else's recipe.
low: Say your pasta is probably the best at the table and offer to cook it for everyone next time.

situation: You're in a weekend pottery class, and the instructor holds up your bowl as an example for the group.
high: Shrug it off with a smile and point out how much you still want to improve on the glazing.
low: Take the praise with a nod and explain the technique that made your bowl stand out.

situation: You're updating your profile on a professional networking site after finishing a certification course.
high: Add the certification in a brief line and keep the rest of your summary plain.
low: Add the certification with a bold headline calling yourself a top performer in the field.

situation: You are walking to the train station after work and pass a man sitting on the pavement with a paper cup and a handwritten sign.
high: Stop for a moment, say hello, and put some change in his cup before moving on.
low: Keep walking at your usual pace and stay focused on catching your train.

situation: A coworker mentions at lunch that her landlord is selling the building and she has to find a new flat within a month.
high: Ask how she is holding up and offer to send her any rental listings you come across.
low: Say that sounds like a hassle and steer the chat back to the afternoon's project.
flags: situation not in the second person

situation: You are scrolling through the news on your phone and see a report about families displaced by flooding in another region.
high: Read the whole story, then look up a relief fund and send a small donation.
low: Skim the headline and move on to the sports scores and the weather forecast.

situation: At a neighbourhood barbecue, a man you barely know starts describing how tough the past year has been since his hours were cut.
high: Listen closely, ask what has been hardest, and mention you are around if he needs anything.
low: Nod politely, then excuse yourself to refill your drink and talk to someone else.

situation: While waiting in line at the supermarket, you notice the person ahead counting coins and putting a few items back because they are short.
high: Offer to cover the difference so they can keep everything in their basket.
low: Wait patiently and look at your phone until the line starts moving again.

situation: Your landlord sends a flat-pack bookshelf to your door, and the instructions are missing a page.
high: Start building it yourself, working out the missing steps from the other diagrams as you go.
low: Set the pieces aside until you can get the full instructions or have someone come help with it.

situation: Your manager asks if anyone can take over a client presentation next week, and the topic is new to you.
high: Volunteer to take it on, trusting you can learn the material in time.
low: Hold back and suggest someone who already knows the topic should present it.

situation: Your kitchen tap starts dripping on a Saturday morning, and you have a basic toolkit at home.
high: Watch a short tutorial and try replacing the washer yourself.
low: Book a plumber to look at it, even if it means waiting a few days.

situation: You're planning a week-long trip abroad with two friends, and nothing has been booked yet.
high: Offer to arrange the flights, lodging and daily plans, confident it will come together.
low: Suggest splitting the planning into small parts, or using a travel agent to sort the details.

situation: You've joined a community pottery class, and the teacher offers a harder technique to anyone who wants to try it.
high: Sign up for the harder technique, expecting to get the hang of it with practice.
low: Stick with the basics for now until you feel surer of your hands.

situation: You get home from the grocery store with several bags and a pile of mail you picked up on the way in.
high: Put each item away in its usual cupboard right away and sort the mail into a tray by the door.
low: Set everything down on the counter and deal with it later, once you have eaten and settled in.

situation: You have just finished a long afternoon of painting at your kitchen table, and the supplies are spread all across it.
high: Rinse the brushes, close the paint tubes and return every item to its labelled box before you stand up.
low: Leave the supplies out where they are so you can pick up again tomorrow without setting up.

situation: You are packing a suitcase the evening before a week-long trip to visit a friend.
high: Lay out the clothes by category and fold them into the case in neat, planned stacks.
low: Pull items from the wardrobe and drop them into the case in whatever order they come to hand.

situation: You have finished a big project at work and your desk is covered with notes, cups and loose papers.
high: Spend a few minutes filing the papers, wiping the surface and lining up your pens before you leave.
low: Grab what you need for tomorrow and head out, leaving the rest of the pile as it is.

situation: You come back from a weekend hike with a muddy backpack, boots and a bag of damp gear.
high: Unpack everything straight away, hang the damp items to dry and put the gear back on its shelf.
low: Drop the backpack and boots by the entrance and unpack them when you next need something.

situation: You told a coworker last week that you'd look over her slide deck before Friday's meeting. Thursday evening arrives and a friend invites you to a last-minute dinner.
high: Decline the dinner and spend the evening going through her slides as you said you would.
low: Go to the dinner and send her a quick note saying you'll skim the slides if time allows.

situation: You're at a self-checkout in a supermarket, and the sign says the express lane is for 10 items or fewer. You have about 14 items and the regular lanes are long.
high: Join the longer regular line so you stay within the posted limit.
low: Use the express lane anyway since it's quick and nobody is policing it.

situation: You signed up to bring snacks to your weekend hiking group, but the morning of the hike you're running late and the store is out of your way.
high: Make the detour to the store so you bring what you signed up for.
low: Grab whatever is already in your kitchen and head straight to the trailhead.

situation: You're assembling a bookshelf, and the instructions say to follow the steps in order and tighten all the bolts at the end. You can see an easier way to do it by tightening as you go.
high: Follow the printed order of steps and tighten the bolts at the end as directed.
low: Do it your own way and tighten each bolt as you go along.

situation: You borrowed a neighbour's ladder and said you'd return it by Sunday. Sunday comes, it's raining, and you're comfortable on the sofa.
high: Put on a jacket and carry the ladder back to your neighbour's, as you promised.
low: Stay in and text your neighbour that you'll bring it over sometime in the next few days.

situation: You've just finished a report at work that meets everything your manager asked for, and it's an hour before you normally leave.
high: Use the extra time to add a comparison chart and a short summary of next steps.
low: Send it off as it is and head home at your usual time.

situation: You've started a weekly evening pottery class where the teacher says people can work at whatever pace they like.
high: Set yourself a goal of making a full matching dinner set by the end of term.
low: Make whatever appeals to you each week and see where it ends up.

situation: You're helping organise a friend's birthday dinner at a restaurant, and the booking is already confirmed for the right number of people.
high: Plan a small extra, such as a personalised menu and a toast, to make the evening stand out.
low: Leave it there and just turn up on the night with everyone else.

situation: You're doing a weekend run in a local park and have been going for about twenty minutes at an easy pace.
high: Pick up the pace to try to beat your previous best time for the loop.
low: Keep jogging at the same easy pace until you reach the end of the loop.

situation: You're learning a new language on a phone app, and you've completed today's lesson with a few minutes to spare.
high: Start the next lesson to get further ahead of your weekly target.
low: Close the app and do something else until tomorrow's lesson.

situation: You planned to spend Saturday morning cleaning out the garage, but the weather is beautiful and a friend texts about heading to the lake.
high: Finish the garage first as planned, then message your friend to see if they're still around in the afternoon.
low: Tell your friend you're in, and leave the garage for some other weekend when the weather's worse.

situation: You have a report due Friday afternoon, and it's now Monday morning with nothing written yet.
high: Block out an hour each morning this week and write a section at a time until it's done.
low: Wait until you feel in the right headspace and write most of it in one long push closer to the deadline.

situation: You signed up for a gym class that starts at 6:30 a.m. tomorrow, and tonight there's a good show on that runs late.
high: Turn the show off at your usual bedtime and set out your gym bag so you can make the class.
low: Watch the full episode and decide in the morning whether you feel like going to the class.

situation: You're at your desk about to begin a long task, and your phone shows a few new notifications and a funny video link from a coworker.
high: Put your phone in a drawer and work for a set stretch before looking at anything.
low: Open the video and check the notifications first, then ease into the task when you get to it.

situation: You're setting up a budget to save for a trip next summer, and you've just seen a sale on a gadget you'd enjoy.
high: Skip the gadget so you stay on the monthly savings amount you set for yourself.
low: Buy the gadget now and work out the savings for the trip later on with whatever's left.

situation: You spot a secondhand road bike online that's priced well below similar ones, and the seller says two other people have asked about it.
high: Ask the seller for the service history and a day to look it over before deciding.
low: Message back right away that you'll take it and arrange to pick it up today.

situation: Your team lead offers you a role on a new project starting next month, and wants an answer by the end of the meeting.
high: Ask for a couple of days to go over the details and think through the workload.
low: Say yes on the spot and work out the details once the project starts.

situation: You're at a hardware store about to start painting your living room, and the staff show you a dramatic new colour you hadn't considered.
high: Buy a small sample tin, test it on the wall, and look at it for a few days.
low: Switch to the new colour and buy enough tins to do the whole room today.

situation: On holiday in a new city, you have a free afternoon and a friend suggests booking a last-minute day trip to a town you know little about.
high: Look up the route, return times and reviews before agreeing to book.
low: Book the tickets straight away and see how the day unfolds.

situation: You've been given a new flat-pack wardrobe to assemble, and the instructions are thick with diagrams and many small parts.
high: Lay out all the pieces and read through every step before picking up a screwdriver.
low: Start screwing the first pieces together and check the instructions only when stuck.
